external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A member of the grocery loyalty programme.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop

external_entities.name: member phone
external_entities.description: A phone used by a member to run the mobile app and retain a refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile app used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members, issues authorization codes, refresh tokens and access tokens, and handles partner consent.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and handles gift-card redemptions.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application used to close a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

processes.name: member browser
processes.description: A browser used for member sign-in and for returning an authorization code to a partner app.
processes.source_excerpt: The member's sign-in on the authorization server is kept in a cookie for thirty days.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request to the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API using an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: access token and rewards API request

data_flows.name: use browser
data_flows.description: A member uses a browser to sign in and approve consent.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server sign-in page and consent screen.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests containing its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret and token request

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server reads and writes member identity and authorization data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: disconnect partner
data_flows.description: The mobile app causes a partner app's refresh token to be deleted from the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app, which deletes that app's refresh token from the identity database.

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: take access tokens
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.data_description: member account closure and refresh-token records

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's own cloud account where the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: member phones
trust_boundaries.description: The members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud account.

trust_boundaries.name: partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers run by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member identity information, password hashes, tokens and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because request headers may contain credentials and requests may contain member-related data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request, headers included, is written to the API log store.
